paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the values of two different methods across a varying number of examples. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Examples," featuring a linear scale ranging from 0 to 8 with numerical tick marks spaced every 2 units. The y-axis is labeled "minFDE$_{20}$ ($\leftarrow$)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 15.50 to 19.00, with numerical tick marks at intervals of 0.50. The plot contains two lines. The first line, labeled "ST-ES" in the legend, is a solid blue line with circular markers. It begins at approximately 18.98 at x=0, experiences a sharp decline to roughly 16.48 at x=1, and then continues to decline more gradually, reaching about 15.65 at x=6. It shows a slight increase to roughly 15.70 at x=7 before dropping to its lowest point of approximately 15.55 at the end of the x-axis (x=8). The second line, labeled "Random," is a solid orange line with circular markers. This line starts at exactly 18.50 at x=0, drops to approximately 17.65 at x=1, and then follows a steady, gradual decline to reach a minimum value of roughly 17.13 at x=5. After this low point, the line steadily increases across the remainder of the axis, ending at a value of approximately 17.45 at x=8.
